source_text: Dixerat quidem, ut David propheta testis est, insipiens in corde suo, quia non esset Deus [n7] , non tamen dixerat, quia esset quidem, sed tamen iniustus Deus; ita concinenter totius naturae voce resonabat inseparabiliter Deo adhaerere iustitiam, ut facilius inveniretur, qui substantiam eius quam qui aequitatem negaret; potuit exsistere, qui putaret non esse, quod non videbat, non fuerat tamen inventus, qui diceret iniquum, quod divinum esse credebat.
pass_a_gloss: The fool had indeed said, as the prophet David is witness, in his heart that God was not; yet he had not said that God indeed was, but nevertheless an unjust God; so concordantly the voice of all nature was resounding that justice clings inseparably to God, that more easily one would be found who would deny his substance than who would deny his fairness; there could exist one who thought that what he did not see was not, yet there had not been found one who would call unjust what he believed to be divine.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: As the prophet David testifies, the fool did indeed say in his heart that there was no God (Psalm 14:1; Psalm 53:1; LXX/Vulgate Psalms 13:1; 52:1). Yet he did not say that God existed but was unjust. The voice of all nature declared in such harmony that justice belongs inseparably to God that someone denying his existence was more readily found than someone denying his fairness. Someone could arise who thought that what he could not see did not exist; no one had yet been found who called unjust what he believed to be divine.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
